name: 15f grpo group advantages
title: GRPO scores each sample against the rest of its group
subtitle: Prompt: what is 17 × 24? The checker compares the final answer with 408. Group size G = 4.

steps.caption: The policy writes four answers to the same prompt. No critic network is trained, so the group itself has to say which answers were better than usual.
A program checks each final answer against 408. Only sample 1 is right, so the rewards are 1, 0, 0, 0. No reward model is involved.
The group mean is 0.25 and the standard deviation is the square root of 0.25 × 0.75, which is 0.433. The mean plays the role a critic's value estimate would.
Sample 1 gets (1 − 0.25) / 0.433 = +1.732 and each wrong sample gets (0 − 0.25) / 0.433 = −0.577. The advantages sum to zero, and the rare success gets the large push.
A second prompt that the model already solves: all four samples are right, so every reward is 1.
steps.heading: When all rewards tie

steps.caption: Equal rewards give zero advantage for every sample, so this group gives no reward gradient. An all-wrong group behaves the same way.
